meta.description: One recorded episode of a Drosophila male-CNS visual sub-circuit (frozen connectome, fitted interface only) playing Flappy Bird, alongside enough level and physics data for a browser to replay the identical level and let a human play it too. `fly` gives the bird's exact per-frame trajectory and flap decisions; `activity` gives per-frame spike counts for a subset of neurons (all 10 output-seed descending neurons plus the highest-traffic interneurons this episode); `gf` isolates the two DNp01 giant-fiber neurons (this model has no adaptation, so they cannot habituate). See docs/RESULTS.md for what is frozen vs fitted.

schema.meta.connectome: str, connectome name/version, or 'SYNTHETIC PLACEHOLDER (...)' when this replay was NOT recorded from the real sub-circuit -- check meta.is_real_connectome before making any provenance claim in a UI.
schema.meta.is_real_connectome: bool, true only when this episode ran on the real MaleCNS sub-circuit (network 'real' with the expected neuron count). A page must not claim a real fly brain when false.
schema.meta.n_neurons: int, neuron count in the recorded network (read from the network file).
schema.meta.n_edges: int, nonzero-edge count in the recorded network (read from the network file).
schema.meta.network: str, the run's network id ('real' or 'control_NN').
schema.meta.run_seed: int, the CMA-ES run seed that produced best_x.
schema.meta.git_commit: str, git commit of the training run (from its config.json).
schema.meta.heldout_mean: float, the run's held-out mean score over its 20 held-out seeds.
schema.meta.game_seed: int, the held-out seed used for this specific episode.
schema.meta.score: int, the fly's final score this episode.
schema.meta.frames: int, number of frames recorded (episode length; capped at config.max_frames).
schema.meta.description: str, one-paragraph plain-language summary of this file.
schema.meta.context: object: where this run sits among all finished runs. real_runs, this_run_rank (1 = best held-out mean), real_median, real_runs_at_or_below_3_3, control_runs, control_best, and rule_baseline (held-out mean of a brain-free one-line rule on the same information the interface gives the brain -- see docs/RESULTS.md, C1).
schema.config: object, every GameConfig field (docs/PLAN.md Step 4), all numbers. config.frame_ms is simulated BRAIN time per frame (25 ms), not a display frame rate.
schema.level: array of {x0, gap_centre}, ordered by x0 ascending. x0 is the pipe's left edge at frame 0 (Game.reset(), before any step()). Pipe position at recorded array index i (0-based) is x0 - (i + 1) * config.pipe_speed. Enough pipes are included to cover config.max_frames.
schema.fly.bird_y: float[frames], rounded to 3 decimals. Post-step bird y each recorded frame.
schema.fly.bird_vy: float[frames], rounded to 3 decimals. Post-step bird vertical velocity.
schema.fly.flap: int[frames], 0/1: whether the brain flapped on that frame. Physics for a flap: it SETS bird_vy to config.flap_velocity (it does not add to it). Per frame, in order: apply flap; vy = min(vy + config.gravity, config.max_fall_speed); y += vy; pipes move left by config.pipe_speed; a pipe scores once, the first frame its right edge (x + pipe_width) is left of config.bird_x - config.bird_radius; death = ceiling (y - r <= 0), floor (y + r >= config.height), or circle-vs-rectangle overlap with either pipe rectangle.
schema.fly.score: int[frames]. Cumulative score after that frame.
schema.activity.ids: int[n_neurons_kept], bodyId of each kept neuron, ordered: the 10 output-seed neurons (network row order), then a sample of input-seed (looming) neurons, then interneurons ranked by total spikes this episode. Group with activity.roles, never by position.
schema.activity.types: str[n_neurons_kept]. For the 10 output seeds: '<DN type>_<L|R>' (e.g. 'DNp01_R'). For all others: the neuron's `type` column value (e.g. 'LC4', 'LPLC2').
schema.activity.counts: int[frames][n_neurons_kept]. Spike count of each kept neuron, per frame.
schema.gf.ids: int[2], bodyId of the two DNp01 neurons (giant-fiber channel), R then L.
schema.gf.counts: int[frames][2]. DNp01 spike counts per frame, R then L.
